evidence: Read engine/review/rolerecords.go lines 168-280 in the worktree. DecodeSweep embeds sweepFile and adds a depth-0 `T4 json.RawMessage` field. That field shadows the promoted SweepFindings.T4, so a record with no t4 gives a nil RawMessage and decodes as two empty non-nil lists. A present t4 goes through DecodeStrict, which rejects unknown members. A null or missing list is refused by the nil checks in decodeSweepT4. Errors are wrapped in ErrInvalidStored at line 272.
Read engine/jsonstrict/jsonstrict.go and engine/review/stored.go. decodeFile checks duplicate keys first, then strict decoding, so a duplicate t4 key or a stray member is refused.

Grepped the engine for readers of the sweep record. DecodeSweep is the only decoder, used at app/recordrole.go:97 and app/needs.go:90, and EncodeSweep is the only encoder. A record stored before T4 keeps its outcome and its candidate ids (Fired is unchanged for old content), and a present t4 is encoded with both lists as arrays.
Read engine/review/sweep.go Leftovers. It matches on the base name suffix, excludes paths in T1.DeletedOrRenamed, deduplicates, sorts and returns a non-nil slice.
The imports for json and jsonstrict already exist in rolerecords.go. I did not run any tests or builds.
